title: What boat actually
_fits Lake Texoma?_
hero.lede: Texoma is big, open and famously windy. At roughly 89,000 acres straddling the Texas–Oklahoma border, it has enough fetch for a calm morning to turn into a two-foot chop by mid-afternoon. That single fact should drive most of your boat-buying decision.

intro.text: This guide walks through how people actually use this lake, what that means for hull type and size, and which boats hold up to a full Texoma season. Written by the team at Big Water Marine in Pottsboro, who sell, service and store boats here year-round.

wind.title: Start with the wind, _not the boat._
wind.lede: Most first-time Texoma buyers shop on layout and upholstery. Then they take delivery in June, head out at 2pm on a Saturday, and discover the lake has other ideas. Wind is the defining characteristic here — it is why sailors love Texoma and why an undersized boat gets old fast.
wind.pullQuote: If a boat is comfortable in Texoma afternoon chop, it will be comfortable almost anywhere you take it.
wind.body: Three things make a boat handle that chop well: **length, weight and hull design**. A longer, heavier boat bridges waves instead of slapping into them. On pontoons, that means the difference between two tubes and three, and whether there is a performance package under the deck. On V-hulls, it means deadrise — the sharper the entry, the softer the ride.

use.title: How do you actually _use the lake?_
use.lede: The boat that wins is the one matched to your real weekends, not your aspirational ones.

callout.title: The size mistake
callout.text: People almost never regret going two feet longer. They regret going two feet shorter almost every windy Saturday. If you are between sizes on Texoma, size up.

winterize.q: Can you winterize my boat at a marina, storage facility or my house?
winterize.a: Yes. Our mobile team travels to marinas, storage facilities and homes across Lake Texoma. Mobile rates apply, plus travel ($75 minimum, $2.50 per mile). Gear lube and impeller work needs the boat on a trailer or lift.

winterize.q: Can I just use a marine heater or lamp instead?
winterize.a: While marine approved bilge heaters are a good idea, they aren’t a substitute for winterization. Power outages, tripped breakers, or temperature swings can still freeze and crack components. Many Texas freeze claims happen because heaters failed during sudden cold snaps or power outage.
{inspectionPoints}. You get a summary report with any recommended maintenance.

winterize.q: When should I book my winterization?
winterize.a: As early as possible — once temperatures dip, appointments fill quickly. We start scheduling in late summer, and prime weeks typically sell out. Don’t wait until the first freeze warning.

winterize.q: Are materials included in the price?
winterize.a: No. Package prices are labor only, for single-engine boats. Materials such as antifreeze, oil, filters, stabilizer and parts are billed separately, and we never do extra work without an estimate first.

boatclub.q: What is Big Water Boat Club?
boatclub.a: A membership that gives you access to Lake Texoma boat rentals at a big discount. Instead of the normal rental rate, members pay {club.discount}% of the posted rate at Lighthouse Resort & Marina.

boatclub.q: How much does it cost to join?
boatclub.a: The initiation fee is ${club.returningInitiation}, discounted to ${club.initiation} for your first membership, plus ${club.monthly} a month, billed quarterly (${club.quarterly}). After that, every boat you book at Lighthouse Resort & Marina is {club.discount}% off the posted rental rate.

boatclub.q: What do I need to join?
boatclub.a: Be {club.minAge} or older, pay the ${club.initiation} initiation fee and your first quarter’s dues (${club.quarterly}), complete the boater safety course at boaters-ed.com, and take the free Intro to Boating on Lake Texoma class from our partner BoaterWise.

boatclub.q: When can I rent a boat? How many reservations can I have?
boatclub.a: There are no restrictions or blackout dates. Rent half days, full days, weekdays, weekends and holidays. Book online or by phone, up to the day of your rental, subject to availability.

boatclub.q: How is Big Water Boat Club different from other boat clubs?
boatclub.a: Many clubs have high buy-ins, expensive monthly fees, membership tiers and reservation limits. Ours is simple: ${club.initiation} to join, ${club.monthly} a month, and {club.discount}% off rentals, plus discounts with affiliated companies and a professional team to help you make the most of every trip.

No. After you join you pay quarterly dues and {club.discount}% of the posted rental rate when you rent. Rates vary by season, weekday or weekend, and holidays: a winter half day at ${club.winterHalfDay} costs a member ${club.winterHalfDayHalf}, and a holiday full day of up to ${club.holidayFullDay} costs a member up to ${club.holidayHalfDay}. Each rental needs a refundable ${club.deposit} damage deposit on a major credit card, and you pay for the fuel you use at the discounted member rate.

Dues are billed quarterly, so the minimum commitment is three months, and you can cancel anytime after that with written notice. If you cancel and rejoin later, the initiation fee is ${club.returningInitiation}.

boatclub.q: Can I buy a boat later?
boatclub.a: Yes. The Member-to-Owner program helps members move into ownership when they’re ready, with Big Water Marine’s sales and service team behind them.

financing.q: What do I need to apply?
financing.a: The standard information any marine lender asks for: identification, income, and details of the boat you’re buying. The application is online and secure, and you’ll usually hear back quickly.
Yes. Repowering an existing boat can be financed the same way as a purchase, which often makes a new engine cheaper per month than continuing to repair an old one.
Yes. Terms vary by the age and value of the boat, so the best step is to apply and let us match you to the right lender.

financing.q: What about commercial or fleet purchases?
financing.a: Fleet and commercial purchases don’t go through our retail lenders. Tell us how the deal is structured and we’ll help you find the right banking partner for it.
Lender policies differ on whether an application triggers a soft or hard inquiry. Ask us before you apply and we’ll tell you what to expect from the lender we’d send you to.

keepboating.q: Should I rent, join Big Water Boat Club, or buy a boat on Lake Texoma?
keepboating.a: It depends on how many days you boat. At about 1–3 days a year, renting keeps it simple. From roughly 2–9 days, Big Water Boat Club saves 50% on every rental for $500 to join and $150 a quarter. At 10 or more days a year, owning your own boat usually makes the most sense. Use the Rent, Join, Own calculator on this page to run your own numbers.

keepboating.q: Can I buy the boat I rented?
keepboating.a: Yes. Previous renters get exclusive discounts on our rental fleet boats, and last year’s boats are offered at big discounts. Same boat, same memories, and no more sold-out weekends.

keepboating.q: How much does Big Water Boat Club save on rentals?
keepboating.a: Members pay 50% of the posted rental rate at Lighthouse Resort & Marina, plus priority booking and access to member-only boats. With a $500 initiation (discounted from $1,000 for your first membership) and $50 a month billed quarterly, most members break even after about two rentals.

keepboating.q: Can I use a renter discount on a new boat?
keepboating.a: Yes. Apply your renter discount to any in-stock model when you buy new, with financing available.

storage.q: Is your storage indoor or outdoor?
storage.a: Outdoor only. We do not offer indoor or covered storage. Boats are kept in secure onsite outdoor storage at our Pottsboro location, and we recommend shrink wrap for anything staying through the winter.

storage.q: How do I get storage included?
storage.a: Our SecurePro winterization package ($1,750 onsite, labor for single-engine boats) includes six months of onsite secure outdoor storage, shrink wrap for boats up to 25 feet, and spring dewinterization.

storage.q: Can I store a boat without buying a winterization package?
storage.a: Call us. Standalone storage depends on current space, which is seasonal and fills up. 903-419-1019 is the fastest way to find out what’s open.
Yes. Shrink wrap is included for boats up to 25 feet in the SecurePro package and is available separately. It’s the single best protection for a boat stored outdoors through a Texoma winter.

storage.q: Can you pick up and deliver my boat?
storage.a: Pickup and delivery options are available. Tell us where the boat is — home, marina or storage facility — and we’ll quote it.

Dewinterization, or spring startup, gets the boat ready to run. It is included in the SecurePro package and available separately at $165 onsite or $215 mobile. It is also required to keep our winterization guarantee valid.

fleetSales.q: Do I have to buy a whole fleet?
fleetSales.a: No. Fleet pricing starts at two boats, gets deeper at four, and reaches wholesale at eight. Plenty of operators start with a pair and build from there.
Yes — rigged, prepped, and water-ready. Delivery anywhere on Lake Texoma is included. Beyond Texoma we’ll quote it at a reasonable rate.

fleetSales.q: What do I do with the boats I’m replacing?
fleetSales.a: Whatever nets you the most. We’ll help you retail them yourself, take them on consignment and handle the sale, or make you a favorable trade on the upgrade — and we’ll tell you honestly which one puts more money back in your pocket.

fleetSales.q: Can you service our existing fleet, even if we didn’t buy it here?
fleetSales.a: Yes. We’re factory-authorized for Mercury, Yamaha, Suzuki and BRP, and our mobile technicians work at your dock or marina.

fleetSales.q: Do you handle off-season storage and winterization?
fleetSales.a: Yes — winterization, shrink wrap, and storage are all handled in-house.
Commercial fleet purchases don’t go through our retail lenders — but we’ll help you find the right banking partner for it. Tell us how the deal is structured and we’ll make the introduction.

Sales is open Tuesday through Saturday, 9am to 5pm. Service is open Tuesday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, and Saturday 8am to 3pm. Both are closed Sunday and Monday.

contact.q: How do I get there from Dallas?
contact.a: Take US-75 north past Sherman and Denison, then head west toward Pottsboro and Lake Texoma. It is roughly 75 miles from Dallas.
Not to browse inventory. Sea trials, demos and service work are scheduled, so call ahead on 903-419-1019 for those.

contact.q: Can you come to my boat instead?
contact.a: Yes. Our mobile technicians work at your dock or marina, which saves hauling the boat to us. Mobile rates apply.

brands.q: Which brands do you sell new?
brands.a: Berkshire and Veranda pontoons, Scout center consoles, and Highfield rigid inflatable boats and tenders. All four are available new at our Pottsboro location.

brands.q: What engines do your boats come with?
brands.a: Suzuki, Yamaha, Mercury and Rotax, depending on model. We are a factory-authorized service center for Mercury, Yamaha, Suzuki and BRP, so whatever you buy, we can service it here.

brands.q: Which brand is best for Lake Texoma?
brands.a: It depends on how you boat. Pontoons suit entertaining and family days in Texoma chop; a Scout center console suits serious fishing; a Highfield RIB suits tenders and fast, rough-water runs. Come tell us how you use the lake.

brands.q: Do you sell used boats from other brands?
brands.a: Yes. Used inventory rotates and has included Trifecta, Carolina Skiff, Monterey and Sea Ray alongside used examples of the brands we carry new.

brands.q: Can I sea trial before I buy?
brands.a: Yes, by appointment. Schedule a demo and feel how the boat handles real Texoma water before you commit.

buyingGuide.q: What size boat is best for Lake Texoma?
buyingGuide.a: For most families, 22 to 25 feet. That range carries a crowd, handles afternoon chop, and still trailers and stores easily. Smaller boats are fine for calm mornings but get uncomfortable when the wind comes up.

buyingGuide.q: Are pontoons safe on a lake this big?
buyingGuide.a: Yes, when they are specified for it. A tritoon with a performance package handles Texoma chop well. A basic two-tube boat is better suited to sheltered water and calm mornings.
On Texoma, tritoon. The third tube adds buoyancy, stability and the ability to carry more power, which together make the difference on a windy afternoon.

buyingGuide.q: What is the best boat for striper fishing here?
buyingGuide.a: A 21 to 24 foot center console. The deep-V entry softens wind chop, and the open deck lets you follow a fish around the boat instead of over the furniture.

buyingGuide.q: Can I see a boat on the water before buying?
buyingGuide.a: Yes, by appointment. Call 903-419-1019 and we will schedule a demo. We would rather you find out on our time than after delivery.

newVsUsed.q: Is it cheaper to own a used boat on Lake Texoma?
newVsUsed.a: Up front, yes. Over a season, less than people expect. Winterization, shrink wrap and storage are priced by length rather than age, so they cost the same on either boat. The real variable is unplanned repairs.

newVsUsed.q: How much does it cost to store a boat for the winter?
newVsUsed.a: Secure outdoor storage is $2 per foot per month for shrinkwrapped boats, and wrap is $25 per foot. A 22-foot boat stored six months comes to about $814 for wrap and storage combined.

newVsUsed.q: Do I have to winterize on Lake Texoma?
newVsUsed.a: Yes, if you want to avoid a cracked block. Our packages start at $335 onsite, and our Guaranteed Winterization means that if your engine does not start in spring because of our process, we make it right at no charge.

newVsUsed.q: Are ex-rental boats a bad buy?
newVsUsed.a: Not necessarily. Fleet boats are maintained on a commercial schedule by factory-authorized technicians, so their service history is usually better documented than a private owner’s. Condition matters more than the badge.

newVsUsed.q: What costs do you not publish?
newVsUsed.a: Insurance, fuel, registration and slip fees, because they depend on your boat’s value, how you use it and who you insure with. Everything we control — service, winterization, storage, detailing — is published rather than quoted after the fact.

faqs.q: Where is Big Water Marine located?
faqs.a: Two locations in Pottsboro, Texas on Lake Texoma. Boat sales are at 50055 N State Hwy 289, open Tuesday through Saturday, 9am–5pm. Service is at 33 Tackle Box Dr, open Tuesday through Friday 8am–5pm and Saturday 8am–3pm. Both reach us at 903-419-1019.

faqs.q: What boat brands do you sell?
faqs.a: Four new brands: Berkshire and Veranda pontoons, Scout center consoles, and Highfield aluminum-hull RIBs and tenders. Boats are rigged with Suzuki, Yamaha, Mercury and Rotax power. Used inventory rotates and has included Trifecta, Carolina Skiff, Monterey and Sea Ray.

faqs.q: Do you sell used boats?
faqs.a: Yes. Used and brokerage boats are listed alongside new inventory, including gently used fleet and rental boats that have been maintained on a commercial service schedule. Current stock is on our inventory page with prices, photos and specs.

faqs.q: Do you take trade-ins?
faqs.a: Yes. We’ll appraise your boat, and final value is confirmed after an in-person inspection. If you’re replacing several boats at once, we’ll also tell you honestly whether trading or retailing them puts more money back in your pocket.

faqs.q: Do you offer financing?
faqs.a: Yes, for retail boat purchases and for repowers, through our lending partners. Applications are handled online. Commercial and fleet purchases don’t run through our retail lenders — for those we’ll help you find the right banking partner.

faqs.q: Will you service an engine you didn’t sell me?
faqs.a: Yes. We service all major outboard brands plus sterndrive and inboard/outboard setups, regardless of where the boat was bought. We’re a factory-authorized service center for Mercury, Yamaha, Suzuki and BRP, so warranty-approved work stays intact.

faqs.q: Do you come to my dock?
faqs.a: Yes. Mobile service brings a certified technician to your dock or marina, which is often the difference between losing a weekend and keeping it. Same-day service is available for routine maintenance. Call 903-419-1019 to schedule.

faqs.q: How much does winterization cost?
faqs.a: Onsite packages start at $335 for FreezeGuard, our essential freeze-protection service, and run to $1,750 for SecurePro, which adds shrink wrap, six months of storage and spring startup. All quotes are labor for single-engine boats; materials are additional, and mobile service is quoted separately.

faqs.q: What is Guaranteed Winterization?
faqs.a: If your engine doesn’t start in spring because of our winterization process, we make it right at no charge. It’s the reason we’d rather do the job properly in autumn than argue about it in April.

faqs.q: Do you offer boat storage?
faqs.a: Yes. Storage is available and is included for six months in our SecurePro winterization package, along with shrink wrap for boats up to 25 feet. Pickup and delivery options are available. Call for current availability, which is seasonal.

faqs.q: What is Big Water Boat Club?
faqs.a: A membership that gives you access to boats on Lake Texoma without owning one — no maintenance, storage or winterizing. Members book the boat they want and we handle the rest.

faqs.q: Do you sell boats to marinas and rental operators?
faqs.a: Yes. Fleet pricing starts at two boats, gets deeper at four, and reaches wholesale at eight. Delivery anywhere on Lake Texoma is included. We also service fleets at your dock, whether or not you bought the boats from us.

faqs.q: Is the trailer included in the price?
faqs.a: All of our boat packages include the trailer unless otherwise specified. If you don’t need one, we can remove it from the estimate.

faqs.q: What fees are not included in the listed price?
faqs.a: Tax, title and license (TTL), freight, prep and doc fee are not reflected in the posted price. We’ll walk you through the full out-the-door number before you commit to anything.

faqs.q: Can I sea trial a boat before buying?
faqs.a: Yes, by appointment. Contact sales to schedule an on-water demo so you can feel how the boat handles Texoma chop before you decide.
